interpretation: 400 rows is not on the useful speed-accuracy frontier if practical rather than near-identity fidelity is the objective.
200, 100 and 50 rows retain very small bounded Richards errors while materially increasing measured acceleration.
25 rows is qualitatively different: coarse-profile head error rises to about 0.0355 cm and theta error to about 0.00158, so it should not be promoted before whole-application characterization.
50 and 100 rows are the primary Phase-2 whole-Hupsel candidates; 200 rows is a conservative bridge/reference candidate.
Timing values are single-run matrix characterization and require paired whole-Hupsel confirmation before practical selection.
next: Run exact whole-Hupsel paired characterization for 200/100/50 rows against analytical baseline, using the uploaded official SWAP 4.3.1 authority. Keep 25 rows as an exploratory lower-bound candidate only if the primary candidates do not expose application instability.
